\label{lemma-shriek-well-defined}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism
of $\textit{FTS}_S$. The functor $f^!$ is, up to canonical isomorphism,
independent of the choice of the compactification.
stage_b_review_note: At line 3768 the source claims compactification-independence of f^! in the named Noetherian finite-type separated situation. The draft spells out j* a_{bar f} and states canonical natural equivalence among ANY two compactifications, with no unconditional identification with the unrestricted adjoint of Rf_*.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Then for *any two* compactifications $j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i$ and proper $\bar f_i:\overline X_i\to Y$ of the same $f$, the exact functors $j_1^*a_{\bar f_1}$ and $j_2^*a_{\bar f_2}$ on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ are canonically naturally isomorphic, compatibly with passing through common dominating compactifications. Thus the upper-shriek functor $f^!$ is defined canonically up to coherent natural isomorphism, independently of the compactification.
hypotheses: S Noetherian; f an S-morphism of separated finite-type S-schemes; two proper compactifications and right adjoints.
conclusions: The compactification-based construction j^*a_{ ar f} is canonically independent of choices.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-upper-shriek-composition}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$
be composable morphisms of $\textit{FTS}_S$. Then there is a canonical
isomorphism $(g \circ f)^! \to f^! \circ g^!$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 3943 the original gives canonical (g∘f)^! -> f^! g^! for composable finite-type separated S maps in the named situation. The preparation retains contravariant order, composition, bounded-below D_QCoh domains and the distinction between isomorphism and strict equality.
statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. Given composable maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, there is a natural isomorphism of exact functors
\[
(g\circ f)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!\circ g^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Z)\longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X),
\]
constructed using compatible proper compactifications and the open-restriction base-change isomorphism for the right adjoints. The isomorphism is independent of these choices; it is not an equality of strictly equal functors.
hypotheses: S Noetherian and composable morphisms in FTS_S; f^! defined by compactification.
conclusions: The upper-shriek construction has a canonical composition isomorphism.

stage_b_review_note: At line 4152 the source explicitly derives a pseudofunctor from compactification-independence and composition isomorphisms. The preparation describes the identity and triple-composition coherence and uses contravariant f^! for categories of bounded-below quasi-coherent-derived complexes.
statement: Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. To each object $X$ of $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ assign the triangulated category $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ and to each map $f:X\to Y$ assign the contravariant exact functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$. Together with the canonical unit isomorphisms $\operatorname{id}_X^!\cong\operatorname{id}$ and the composition isomorphisms $(g\circ f)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}f^!g^!$, these data satisfy the pentagon/associativity coherence condition for any triple of composable morphisms. Hence they form a *contravariant pseudofunctor* from $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ to the $2$-category of triangulated categories and exact functors.
hypotheses: Noetherian base S, FTS_S as specified, upper-shriek functors and their composition isomorphisms.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-map-pullback-to-shriek-well-defined}
In Situation \ref{situation-shriek} let
$f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of $\textit{FTS}_S$. There are canonical maps
$$
\mu_{f, K} :
Lf^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!\mathcal{O}_Y
\longrightarrow
f^!K
$$
functorial in $K$ in $D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $g : Y \to Z$ is another morphism of $\textit{FTS}_S$, then
the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
Lf^*(Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} g^!\mathcal{O}_Z)
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!\mathcal{O}_Y
\ar@{=}[d] \ar[r]_-{\mu_f} &
f^!(Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_Y}^\mathbf{L} g^!\mathcal{O}_Z)
\ar[r]_-{f^!\mu_g} &
f^!g^!K \ar@{=}[d] \\
Lf^*Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} Lf^* g^!\mathcal{O}_Z
\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!\mathcal{O}_Y \ar[r]^-{\mu_f} &
Lf^*Lg^*K \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X}^\mathbf{L} f^!g^!\mathcal{O}_Z
\ar[r]^-{\mu_{g \circ f}} & f^!g^!K
}
$$
commutes for all $K \in D^+_\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_Z)$.
stage_b_review_note: At line 4209 the pinned lemma provides a functorial μ_f:Lf*K⊗f^!O_Y→f^!K for bounded-below K, and a specified two-row composition-compatible square for f,g. The prepared two-path comparison has the same tensor expression, μ_f then f^!μ_g on top, and structure-sheaf μ_f then μ_{g∘f} below.
statement:
Fix a Noetherian base scheme $S$ and let $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ be the category of schemes $T$ with separated finite-type structure map $T\to S$, with $S$-morphisms. For $f:X\to Y$ in this category, choose a *compactification* $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{\bar f}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $\bar f$ proper. Since $\overline X,Y$ are qcqs, the derived pushforward $R\bar f_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{\bar X})\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint $a_{\bar f}$. Define the *upper-shriek* functor $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ by $f^!(K)=j^*a_{\bar f}(K)$, with the canonical identifications between compactifications. This is different in general from the unrestricted right adjoint of $Rf_*$. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, let $\mu_{f,K}:Lf^*K\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}f^!\mathcal O_Y\to f^!K$ be the *upper-shriek projection comparison*, induced from the projection formula and the adjunction counit on a proper compactification, then restricted to the open $X$. Then (1) for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)$ the map $\mu_{f,K}$ is canonical, natural in $K$, and independent of the chosen compactification; (2) if $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ are composable in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ and $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Z)$, the two maps from
\[
Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes_Y^{\mathbf L}g^!\mathcal O_Z)\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}f^!\mathcal O_Y
\]
to $(g\circ f)^!K\simeq f^!g^!K$ agree: one first applies $\mu_{f,Lg^*K\otimes g^!\mathcal O_Z}$ then $f^!(\mu_{g,K})$, and the other uses derived tensor associativity plus $\mu_{f,g^!\mathcal O_Z}$ to obtain $L(g\circ f)^*K\otimes_X^{\mathbf L}(g\circ f)^!\mathcal O_Z$ followed by $\mu_{g\circ f,K}$.
hypotheses: f and g composable in FTS_S; K bounded-below D_QCoh, f^! and projection comparisons defined.
conclusions: Projection comparison exists independently of compactification and coheres with composition.
